questions.q: What does GROUP BY Color, Size group on?
options: Every unique combination of Color AND Size together
Color only, ignoring Size entirely
Size only, ignoring Color entirely
Each column separately, producing two sets of results
questions.explain: Red/Large and Red/Small become two separate groups, each getting its own aggregate values.

questions.q: How does multi-column GROUP BY relate to multi-column DISTINCT (Lesson 9)?
options: They group/deduplicate on the same combination of columns — DISTINCT just removes duplicates, GROUP BY lets you aggregate within each group
They are unrelated concepts with no overlap
DISTINCT can use multiple columns but GROUP BY cannot
GROUP BY always returns fewer rows than DISTINCT on the same columns
questions.explain: Both compare the full combination of selected columns — GROUP BY just adds the ability to aggregate within each resulting group.

questions.q: When a third column is added to a GROUP BY that already has two, what happens to the number of groups?
options: It stays the same or increases — never decreases
It always decreases
It always stays exactly the same
It becomes unpredictable and cannot be reasoned about
questions.explain: Adding a grouping column subdivides existing groups into finer pieces, so the row count can only grow or stay flat.

questions.q: Why does 'SELECT Color, Size, ProductLine, AVG(ListPrice) FROM Production.Product GROUP BY Color, Size;' fail?
options: ProductLine isn't aggregated and isn't included in GROUP BY
AVG cannot be used with a two-column GROUP BY
Color and Size cannot both appear in GROUP BY at once
ListPrice must also appear in GROUP BY
questions.explain: The Lesson 35 rule still applies with multiple grouping columns — every non-aggregated SELECT column must be in GROUP BY.

questions.q: What's the fix for the failing query above?
options: Add ProductLine to the GROUP BY clause as well
Remove AVG(ListPrice) from the SELECT list
Remove GROUP BY entirely
Wrap ProductLine in a WHERE clause instead
questions.explain: GROUP BY Color, Size, ProductLine resolves the error by making every non-aggregated column part of the grouping.
